summary: Selected resolution profiles now cap oversized macOS screen/window frames before they enter the WebRTC source. Scaling preserves aspect ratio and keeps output dimensions even; frames already within the cap are passed through unchanged.

checks.name: Processor reaches legacy and window capture
checks.observation: The processor is registered on VideoProcessingAdapter before capture starts. RTCDesktopCapturer window frames and the macOS 12 screen fallback therefore use the same frame-level cap; ScreenCaptureKit frames already within the limit are unchanged.

checks.name: Screen-share profile tests
checks.observation: All 8 profile, source-dimension, and picker tests passed.

checks.name: Physical legacy display and window capture
checks.observation: No macOS 12 runtime or physical multi-display/window capture session was available in this verification. Sender dimensions, aspect ratio, and every profile still need device acceptance.

remaining: On macOS 12 and a supported modern macOS host, test a selected secondary display and selected window at all nine resolution/frame-rate profiles; verify sender dimensions, aspect ratio, frame rate, and that in-profile frames are not needlessly converted.
